elements.problem: Encoded criteria: BP < 90/60 as (or SBP<90 DBP<60), Pulse > 120, Wheezing, Stridor, Cough, Swelling, Eruption - concepts and thresholds correct. But every item is a sufficient trigger on its own inside one flat 'or': collapse after vaccination plus a cough alone, or DBP 58 with SBP 120, yields probable anaphylaxis. The page presents these as a cluster; a single isolated cough is weak. Swelling is unsited (page: 'like swelling or rash', so general is defensible).

rule_level_problems.problem: No system_priority_evaluation anywhere: the red box 'Treat as anaphylaxis' and the CPR branch (no pulse / not breathing) produce no priority, so a collapsed post-vaccination patient with BP < 90/60 is never escalated.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable anaphylaxis after collapse following vaccination
rule_level_problems.problem: Flat 'or' makes any single delayed-collapse feature sufficient (e.g. cough alone, or diastolic < 60 with normal systolic, or pulse 121 in an anxious patient) for probable anaphylaxis; the page's delayed-collapse picture is a cluster, and timing/LOC duration that would anchor it are absent.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for collapse following vaccination features
rule_level_problems.problem: check_for omits the page's two key discriminators, timing after vaccination and LOC duration/response to leg-raising (Brief / Prolonged loss of consciousness exist in SNOMED), so neither rule can use them; it also lacks 'unresponsive'.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable fainting episode following vaccination
rule_level_problems.problem: Fainting is defined as the complement of the anaphylaxis rule plus all three vitals present and in range; if any vital is unrecorded neither rule fires. Pulse <= 120 is not on the page (page says pulse may be slow).

summary: The file has no priority evaluation, so neither the red box (treat as anaphylaxis) nor the CPR branch escalates the patient. The anaphylaxis rule fires on any single delayed-collapse feature (e.g. cough alone), and neither rule encodes the page's main discriminators, timing after vaccination and loss-of-consciousness duration, although SNOMED has Brief/Prolonged loss of consciousness. Concepts and thresholds that are encoded (BP < 90/60, pulse > 120, wheeze/stridor/cough/swelling/rash, Syncope probable) are otherwise correct.
